title: COVID Booster Shots: CDC Recommends Narrower Use
text:
The CDC is currently re-evaluating its recommendations for COVID-19 boosters , specifically considering a shift towards a risk-based approach . This article dives into the details of the advisory committee’s discussions, exploring potential changes to the COVID-19 booster guidelines for the upcoming season. Learn about the key factors influencing these decisions and the potential impact on public health.
CDC Panel Considers Narrowing COVID-19 Booster Recommendations Published: 2025-04-16
A general view of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention headquarters in atlanta, Georgia, in September 2014. REUTERS/TAMI CHAPPELL/FILE PHOTO Key Takeaways The CDC’s Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices ( ACIP ) is weighing a risk-based approach to COVID-19 booster recommendations. A risk-based strategy would target vulnerable populations for updated COVID-19 vaccines for the 2025-2026 season. Concerns exist regarding the feasibility and messaging of variable recommendations. The ACIP will vote on formal recommendations in June. The panel is also addressing RSV, chikungunya, meningococcal vaccines, and the ongoing measles outbreak. The COVID-19 Booster Debate The U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention’s (CDC) outside panel of vaccine experts convened Tuesday to discuss possibly narrowing recommendations for COVID-19 booster shots for the upcoming immunization campaign. This marks the first meeting under the new Trump governance.
Risk-Based Approach The central idea is to recommend the updated vaccine only for vulnerable populations at risk of severe COVID-19 for the 2025-2026 season. While most panel members expressed openness to the idea, concerns were raised about practical implementation.
“Even though I’m very much in favor of considering a risk-based approach, I am concerned about the feasibility of it and the message it might be sending,”
Jamie Loehr, panelist
Denise Jamieson, another panel member, highlighted the U.S.’s historical challenges in implementing variable recommendations, noting that COVID-19 remains a leading cause of death among adults and children.
current CDC Recommendations Currently, the agency advises that all individuals aged six months and older receive an updated COVID-19 vaccine, irrespective of prior inoculations.
Economic Implications Citi analysts suggest that a risk-based recommendation could further diminish already declining COVID-19 vaccine sales for pharmaceutical companies like Pfizer and Moderna.
Other Vaccines and Outbreaks The Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices (ACIP) is also considering recommendations for vaccines targeting:
respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) Chikungunya (a mosquito-borne disease) Meningococcal disease Additionally, the panel is addressing the ongoing U.S. measles outbreak, which has affected over 700 individuals this year, primarily among unvaccinated residents in Texas and New Mexico.
Meeting Delay and HHS Leadership The meeting faced an abrupt delay in February, shortly after Robert F. Kennedy Jr.,known for his vaccine skepticism,assumed leadership of the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS). The CDC, a part of HHS, cited the need for public comment as the reason for the postponement.
“Today’s long-delayed ACIP meeting harks what we think are early indications of a more relaxed CDC under (kennedy’s) purview of the HHS,”
Citi analysts
CDC Leadership Vacuum The CDC currently lacks a confirmed director. President Donald Trump’s nomination of susan Monarez is pending senate confirmation after he withdrew the nomination of Dave Weldon, a former Republican congressman and vaccine critic.
An HHS spokesperson indicated that CDC Chief of Staff Matthew Buzzelli would provide input on the recommendations in the interim.
